newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Budget changes impact U.Utilities.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Budget changes impact U.Utilities.

text.p: British multi-utility United Utilities may see an extra 10 million stg in tax in 2000 as a result of changes to capital allowances announced in the UK Budget on Tuesday, chief executive Brian Staples said.
"Undoubtedly there will be a significant impact...we were disappointed," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Staples said the tax impact would be rising from 2000.
"The impact of the change is later rather than sooner," he said.

Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke said capital allowances on long-term fixed assets with a working life of over 25 years would be cut to six percent from 25 percent for many businesses spending over 100,000 stg a year on such assets.
Staples said there could also be an impact on customers from the tax change.
"I think the regulator would have to take (the tax change) into account" at the next reviews for water and electricity prices, scheduled for 1999, he added.
